facts: Third quarter revenue totaled $399 million, with year-over-year sales decline driven by lower end market demand in certain North American industrial markets.
Adjusted EPS was $0.65 per diluted share in Q3 2025, compared to $0.66 in Q1 and $0.75 in Q2 of this year.
The company generated EBITDA of $34.2 million in the quarter, representing an 8.6% EBITDA margin, with trailing 12-month EBITDA totaling $140 million.
Fourth quarter free cash flow is expected to range between $45 million to $55 million, with full year free cash flow estimated between $10 million to $20 million.
Capital equipment backlog totaled $185 million as of September 30, an increase of 28% compared to year-end, with the company expecting record annual bookings exceeding $200 million.

The company refinanced both its senior notes and revolving credit facility, extending maturity dates by 5 years, incurring $2 million in bond-related expenses that reduced GAAP earnings by $0.11 per share.
A $47 million order from a major steel producer for induction slab heating equipment will have 3 of 5 pieces of equipment recognized in 2026 and the remaining 2 in 2027.
Full year 2025 guidance includes net sales of $1.600 billion to $1.620 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.70 to $2.90 per diluted share.
The Assembly Components segment is currently launching over $50 million of incremental business across all product lines throughout 2026.
The company expects $35 million to $45 million of debt reduction in Q4 from free cash flow generation.

BARK guided FY2027 revenue of $325–340 million (down from $394.8M in FY26) and adjusted EBITDA of $7–10 million, a meaningful step-up from FY26's $0.2M, with Q1 FY27 revenue guided to $77–79M and EBITDA of $0–1M.
The Board authorized a $40 million share repurchase program to be funded by ongoing free cash flow, the first such program signaling confidence at current stock levels.

Full-year FY26 revenue declined to $394.8M from $484.2M, with Q4 revenue of $86.6M versus $115.4M prior year, reflecting a deliberate $24M+ year-over-year cut in marketing spend (FY26 marketing was $59.2M).
Management is sunsetting the Kibble and toppers product lines due to inadequate returns, reallocating capital to higher-return categories to simplify the business and improve profitability.

D2C revenue is expected to decline year-over-year in 1H FY27 before stabilizing in 2H and returning to growth, as the company enters FY27 with a smaller but higher-quality subscriber base showing improved retention and AOV (D2C gross margin rose 200+ bps to 68%).
Commerce and BARK Air are expected to collectively exceed $100M in FY27 revenue, with Commerce alone projected to grow to roughly 25% of total revenue versus 18% in FY26.
BARK Air revenue more than doubled to over $12.4M in FY26 with 90% utilization, but management is prioritizing unit economics over growth and does not expect significant revenue growth in FY27.
Q4 Commerce revenue fell 18.3% year-over-year to $12.5M due to timing of retail shipments, though full-year Commerce grew modestly to $59.9M (Matt cited $70M including a different segmentation).

The company ended FY26 debt-free with $19M cash and $75.5M inventory (down ~$13M YoY), and expects an additional $12.1M in IEEPA tariff refunds ($7.1M tied to FY26 COGS, $5M to FY27) to be recognized once eligible.
BARK diversified its toy supply chain away from near-total China reliance into multiple Southeast Asian countries and South America, enabling rapid failover if new China tariffs emerge.
IFF's net debt to credit adjusted EBITDA improved from 3.8x at the end of 2024 to 2.6x at the end of 2025, with gross debt decreasing by nearly $3 billion to approximately $6 billion.

Full year 2026 guidance calls for sales of $10.5 billion to $10.8 billion (1% to 4% comparable currency-neutral growth) and EBITDA of $2.05 billion to $2.15 billion (3% to 8% comparable currency-neutral growth).
Full year 2025 free cash flow was $256 million, including approximately $300 million of Reg G-related charges primarily driven by divestiture activities and a $166 million working capital outflow.
IFF formally launched the sale process for its Food Ingredients business approximately two weeks prior to the call, with strong interest from both strategic buyers and financial sponsors.

Health & Biosciences delivered Q4 EBITDA of $155 million, a 20% year-over-year increase, while the health sub-segment remained down low single digits and is expected to return to growth in the second half of 2026.

The company invested approximately $100 million in 2025 into innovation capabilities in high-growth, high-margin categories, with benefits expected to materialize in the second half of 2026 and more fully in 2027.
Incremental margins on volume growth are approximately 30% to 35% depending on the business segment, and 2026 growth is expected to be primarily volume-driven with pricing slightly down.

The Taste segment delivered Q4 EBITDA of $94 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, driven by high single-digit sales growth in North America from new wins, favorable net pricing, and cost discipline.

IFF returned $409 million to shareholders through dividends and $38 million through share repurchases in 2025, with a minimum annual share buyback target of $80 million to $100 million to offset dilution.

Q1 2026 is expected to show muted sales and only modest EBITDA growth versus a like-for-like Q1 2025 base of approximately $505 million (adjusted for divestitures), with year-over-year growth expected to progressively improve each quarter.
Q4 2025 revenue was approximately $2.55 billion with constant currency growth of 3.1%, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Full year fiscal 2025 delivered constant currency revenue growth of 2.1%, which was 60 basis points above the high end of guidance provided a year ago.
Record adjusted free cash flow of $626 million for fiscal 2025 represented a 32% increase (over $150 million) compared to the prior year.

The company returned $258 million to shareholders in fiscal 2025, including $169 million in share repurchases (approximately 3.6 million shares at an average price of $47) and $89 million in dividends.
A $1.52 billion noncash goodwill impairment charge was recorded in Q4, reflecting the trading range of the stock during the quarter.
The iX suite AI platform exited fiscal 2025 with over $60 million in annualized AI revenue and reached breakeven profitability.
Fiscal 2026 guidance includes reported revenue of $10.035 billion to $10.180 billion, implying constant currency growth of 1.5% to 3%.
Net debt was reduced by approximately $184 million during fiscal 2025 to $4.311 billion at year-end.
Banking, financial services and insurance clients grew 11% on a constant currency basis in Q4, the strongest performing vertical.
The company reduced expenditures on non-billable resources and infrastructure by close to $100 million on a run rate basis exiting Q1 2026.

Q1 2026 revenue was $336.6 million, up 2% year-over-year, but would have grown low double digits absent IRA-mandated price declines, which reduced pricing on Guardian's IRA-impacted branded drug mix by approximately 60%.

Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% year-over-year to $29.8 million (8.8% margin), or 14% growth and 8% margin excluding a $3 million discrete benefit from favorable payer dynamics and a manufacturer inventory credit tied to the IRA.
Gross profit rose 19% year-over-year to $76 million (22.7% margin), with the IRA representing an approximate $10 million headwind that management offset through proactive payor renegotiations.

Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $123–$127 million from $120–$124 million to reflect the $3 million discrete benefit, while revenue guidance was maintained at $1.40–$1.42 billion.
Total residents grew 10% year-over-year to approximately 207,000 (with assisted living ~70% of mix), and script volumes also increased 10% year-over-year.

SG&A included a $3.2 million legal expense (added back to adjusted EBITDA) related to payor reimbursement disputes, and a post-quarter settlement will generate an $8.5 million cash payment recognized as Q2 other income (excluded from adjusted EBITDA).
Cash ended the quarter at $65 million (flat with year-end) after absorbing a one-time IRA-related working capital impact, which accounted for roughly half of the working capital used in the quarter.

Acquisitions completed over the past two years dampened consolidated EBITDA margins by approximately 80 basis points, with management expecting a similar drag to persist through 2026 and 2027 as new deals are added.

Guardian completed a nondilutive secondary offering of 6.9 million Class A shares (including full overallotment) priced at $31 per share, and filed a new shelf registration with no current plans to utilize it.

Management flagged potential headwinds including elevated fuel costs (up to a few million dollars annually) and modestly higher labor costs from regional infrastructure investments, while noting Guardian holds only ~13–14% market share with substantial M&A pipeline runway.
Q3 2025 revenues were $202.7 million, with non-GAAP gross margins of 41%, up 250 basis points from 38.5% in Q2 2025.
Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $0.33, which was $0.04 above the high end of the outlook range of $0.21 to $0.29.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $210 million plus or minus $5 million, with non-GAAP gross margin expected at 42% plus or minus 150 basis points.
HBM revenue was approximately $40 million in Q3, close to the previous high, with most sequential DRAM growth driven by HBM.
The company continues to experience a 150 to 200 basis point negative impact on gross margins from tariffs.
Cash expenditures for the Farmers Branch, Texas manufacturing facility are expected to be between $140 million and $170 million over 2026.
Free cash flow was $19.7 million in Q3 compared to negative $47.1 million in Q2, with total cash and investments reaching $266 million at quarter end.
A recently completed headcount reduction is expected to provide approximately $1 million in cost savings in Q4 and about $1.5 million on an ongoing basis thereafter.
The company's largest CPU customer was not a 10% customer in Q3, indicating a significant revenue decline from that customer.
The company expects initial Farmers Branch capacity to come online late in 2026 with the majority of capacity coming online in 2027.

The FCC formally sent a draft Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) focused on PNT technology and solutions to the White House OMB earlier in March 2026, which the company describes as a critical step in the regulatory process.
NextNav finished Q4 2025 with approximately $152 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments.
A significant number of warrants expiring in 2026 have the potential to deliver over $200 million in additional capital depending on stock price performance.
In Q4 2025, NextNav recognized approximately $48 million in noncash losses associated with the change in fair value of derivative and warrant liabilities.
The net loss for Q4 2025 was roughly $68 million, driven primarily by noncash derivative and warrant liability losses.
NextNav has begun operating what it describes as the world's first 5G-powered PNT network under an FCC experimental license in a defined geographic location, independent of the FCC's NPRM process.
NextNav announced an expanded partnership with Japan's MetCom, which has licensed NextNav's technology to power new terrestrial timing services in major Japanese metropolitan areas.
The company's proposed solution does not require taxpayer funding and management believes it can be made available during the current administration.
NextNav CEO Mariam Sorond joined the CTIA Board of Directors, positioning the company alongside major telecommunications industry leaders.

Lisa Hook was appointed as the Board's new Lead Independent Director, bringing experience as former CEO of publicly traded Neustar and expertise at the intersection of technology, telecommunications, and national security.
Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $1.16 billion, exceeding guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.58 up 13% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 bps to 17.6%.

IET delivered record bookings of $4.9 billion (third consecutive quarter above $4 billion) with a 1.5x book-to-bill, driving record RPO of $33.1 billion and IET EBITDA growth of 35% YoY to $678 million at a 20.2% margin (+310 bps).

Power Systems generated $1.4 billion in Q1 orders (~30% of total IET orders), including a 1 GW data center award, 25 BRUSH generators for Boom Supersonic (1.21 GW), and management estimates the behind-the-meter market reaching $60 billion by 2030.
LNG equipment orders totaled $1.2 billion in Q1, highlighted by a QatarEnergy award for 2 mega trains on North Field West (16 MTPA) including 6 Frame 9 turbines and 12 centrifugal compressors.
Management raised confidence that the Horizon 2 IET order target will exceed $40 billion by 2028, supported by structural energy security demand.

Baker Hughes expects approximately $3 billion in gross divestiture proceeds in 2026 from Waygate Technologies, the HMH IPO, PSI sale to Crane, and the SPC/Cactus JV, exceeding its $1 billion incremental divestment target ahead of schedule.

The Middle East conflict has taken ~10% of global oil volumes and 20% of worldwide LNG capacity offline, leading the company to revise its 2026 global upstream spending outlook to modestly below prior low-single-digit decline expectations.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for company revenue of $6.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.13 billion, with IET EBITDA of $670 million and OFSE EBITDA of $540 million on revenue of $3.2 billion, assuming Middle East revenue declines more than 20% sequentially.

Full-year 2026 guidance is maintained but expected to land slightly below the midpoint, with OFSE EBITDA likely at the low end of its $2.325 billion range and IET EBITDA at least the $2.7 billion midpoint.

Q1 free cash flow was $210 million, the balance sheet strengthened with net debt/EBITDA at 0.3x and a $14.8 billion cash position following a $6.5 billion U.S. bond and €3 billion inaugural European bond issuance to fund the Chart acquisition (expected to close in Q2 with $325 million targeted cost synergies).
Full year 2025 U.S. cabozantinib franchise net product revenues grew 17% year-over-year to approximately $2.12 billion.
Global cabozantinib franchise net product revenues generated by Exelixis and its partners were approximately $2.89 billion for full year 2025 and $754 million in Q4 2025.
Fourth quarter 2025 U.S. cabo franchise net product revenues were $547 million, representing 6% year-over-year growth.
CABOMETYX U.S. net product revenues exceeded $100 million for the neuroendocrine tumor indication in 2025, its first year on the market for that indication.
Gross to net for the cabozantinib franchise in Q4 2025 was 28.5%, lower than Q3 2025, and full year 2026 gross to net is estimated to be between 31% and 32%.

During fiscal year 2025, Exelixis repurchased $954 million of outstanding common stock, retiring approximately 24 million shares at an average price of $39.61, with approximately $590 million remaining under the $750 million repurchase authorization.
Cash and marketable securities as of December 31, 2025, were approximately $1.66 billion.
The FDA accepted the NDA submission for zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab in third-line plus CRC with a PDUFA target action date of December 3, 2026.
CABOMETYX TRx volume grew 15% in Q4 2025 versus Q4 2024, outpacing the oral TKI market basket growth rate of 7%, with TRx market share increasing from 43% to 46%.

Top line results from STELLAR-304, the pivotal trial of zanzalintinib plus nivolumab versus sunitinib in non-clear cell RCC, are expected around mid-2026 and could lead to a second NDA filing for zanzalintinib.
Full year 2025 revenue was $203.7 million, representing over 340% growth year-over-year and falling within the company's original guidance range.
Contract backlog reached $1.3 billion as of December 31, 2025, representing 3x growth versus the prior year and 42% sequential growth from Q3.
Full year 2025 GAAP gross margin improved to 23.6%, up 10 percentage points from 13.4% in 2024, roughly 2x the 5%-12% industry comps.
Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $9.8 million compared to a loss of $13.4 million in the prior year quarter.
The company closed a $300 million non-dilutive preferred equity fund with OIC, enabling $1 billion to $1.2 billion of total CapEx for Asset Vault projects.

The company completed a $150 million convertible senior notes offering in February 2026, upsized from $125 million, with proceeds partly used to repay $45 million in higher-cost debt and a capped call resulting in an implied conversion price of $8.12 per share.
Contracted megawatts grew to 540 MW, expected to deliver $130 million to $150 million in EBITDA over the next 18 to 36 months.

For full year 2026, the company is guiding revenue of $225 million to $300 million (approximately 30% growth at the midpoint), gross margin of 15% to 25%, and year-end cash of $150 million to $200 million.

The Calistoga and Cross Trails Asset Vault projects are operational and expected to generate $10 million in annualized recurring adjusted EBITDA, with Asset Vault Fund 1 expected to scale to $100 million to $150 million in recurring adjusted EBITDA by year-end 2029.
The company's developed pipeline exceeds $3 billion associated with 1.8 gigawatts of capacity, and it targets over 3 gigawatts and $1.5 billion-plus in EBITDA by 2030.
Iridium grew full year 2025 operational EBITDA 5% year-over-year to $495.3 million and generated pro forma free cash flow of $296 million.

For 2026, Iridium is guiding service revenue growth of flat to up 2% and OEBITDA of $480 million to $490 million, which includes a $17 million negative impact from switching annual incentive compensation from a cash/equity mix to fully cash.
Iridium projects 2026 pro forma free cash flow of $318 million, representing a 66% OEBITDA-to-free-cash-flow conversion rate and approximately 16% free cash flow yield.
Iridium expects new products being introduced in 2026—including NTN Direct, a new PNT ASIC, and a new IoT device—to represent more than $200 million in revenue opportunity by the end of the decade.

PNT services are expected to generate at least $100 million in annual revenue for Iridium by the end of the decade, and the company is developing a quantum-safe cybersecurity service targeting the $20 billion identity verification market.

Iridium has secured more than $1 billion in U.S. government awards over the last 5 years and has been selected for the Missile Defense Agency's SHIELD (Golden Dome) contract, with the national security addressable market representing a multibillion-dollar opportunity.
Commercial IoT revenue grew 11% in Q4 2025, with more than 30 new IoT products certified and approximately 40 new partners added during the year.

Broadband revenue declined 10% for full year 2025 due to migration from primary to companion/backup plans, and the company expects the decline rate to moderate in 2026 partly due to a replacement opportunity across an estimated 130,000-140,000 legacy Inmarsat C terminals.

Iridium closed 2025 with net leverage of 3.4x OEBITDA and expects to delever to approximately 3x by year-end 2026, with a long-term goal of below 2x, and maintains a cumulative free cash flow outlook of $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion through 2030.

Iridium retired approximately 6.8 million shares at an average price of $27.07 in 2025 but has paused its share repurchase program, while the company expects the Board to again approve a dividend increase in 2026 following an average 5% annual increase since 2023.

Gross written premiums increased 24% year-over-year to approximately $217 million in Q1 2026, with Casualty GWP up over 20% to $147 million, Healthcare Liability up 28% to over $30 million, and Professional Liability up 6% to approximately $28 million.
Adjusted net income rose approximately 40% year-over-year to $16 million, with diluted adjusted EPS of $0.48 and adjusted return on average equity of 14.1%.

The combined ratio was 95.3% for the quarter, with a loss ratio of 66.9% (unchanged year-over-year) and an expense ratio of 28.4%, down 2 points from 30.4%, aided by a favorable timing reclassification of deferrable internal costs from operating to acquisition costs.

Baleen generated over $11 million ($11.4M) in premiums, more than 3x the prior year, with new business submissions up over 140%, quotes up over 110%, binds up over 260%, and a new business quote ratio above 75%.
Digital underwriting (Baleen plus Express) represented just under 7% of total Bowhead GWP, with Express contributing over $3 million in premium at an approximately 65% quote ratio.

On May 1 ceded reinsurance renewals, Bowhead increased its quota share treaty from 26% to 33.5% with higher ceding commissions, decreased its excess of loss treaty from 65% to 57.5%, and management expects the changes to be roughly neutral to net income.
Bowhead expanded its agreement with American Family to raise the $1 billion annual premium cap, which it is projected to exceed this year as management guides to around 20% GWP growth in 2026.

Pre-tax net investment income grew approximately 44% year-over-year to $18 million, with a 4.6% book yield, 4.7% new money rate, AA- average credit quality, and duration extending from 3.0 to 3.2 years, targeting closer to 4 years by year-end.

Total equity ended the quarter at $459 million, with diluted book value per share of $13.80, and IBNR represented 91% of total reserves with only ~$600,000 of prior accident year reserve continuation, attributed to timing of premium billing rather than adverse development.

Management is contracting commercial public D&O due to overly aggressive competitor pricing, while continuing to see rate increases in casualty (notably excess casualty, real estate, construction, manufacturing, and hospitality) and characterizing excess casualty as the most favorable segment in the marketplace.
CoreWeave generated more than $5.1 billion of revenue in fiscal year 2025, up 168% year-over-year, making it the fastest cloud in history to reach $5 billion in annual revenue.

Contracted revenue backlog grew to $66.8 billion, an increase of $11.2 billion sequentially and more than $50 billion year-over-year, with every contract for new capacity expected to begin generating revenue by year-end 2026.
The company expects 2026 CapEx of $30 billion to $35 billion, more than double the $14.9 billion spent in 2025, with substantially all of it tied to already signed customer contracts.

Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $12 billion to $13 billion, representing approximately 140% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, with adjusted operating income expected at $900 million to $1.1 billion.
CoreWeave expects to exit 2027 with more than $30 billion of annualized run rate revenue, up from the $17 billion to $19 billion annualized run rate expected at the exit of 2026.

The weighted average interest rate declined by 300 basis points during 2025 (nearly 600 basis points since 2023), representing nearly $700 million in annualized interest savings based on Q4 debt balance.
Average contract length increased from roughly 4 years to roughly 5 years as customers commit foundational AI workloads for longer periods.
Active power reached more than 850 megawatts across 43 data centers at year-end 2025, with the company expecting to double active power capacity to more than 1.7 gigawatts by year-end 2026.

Approximately 80% of CoreWeave Cloud customers paying at least $1 million per year have adopted one or more storage products, and the number of customers committed to spending at least $1 million grew by nearly 150% in 2025.

Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $898 million with a 57% margin, while Q4 net loss was $452 million driven by $388 million in interest expense, and Q1 2026 margins are expected to trough near zero before expanding to low double digits by Q4 2026.
Free cash flow increased 45% year-over-year to $4.9 billion in Q3 2025, with year-to-date free cash flow reaching $14.9 billion.
Wireless net additions hit a record 414,000 in Q3, with total wireless lines approaching 9 million and penetration surpassing 14% of the broadband base.

Connectivity & Platforms EBITDA declined 3.7% in Q3 due to investments in pricing simplification and customer experience, with management expecting this decline to build slightly over the next several quarters.
Broadband subscribers declined 104,000 in the quarter amid an intensely competitive environment.
Theme parks revenue grew 19% and EBITDA grew 13% year-over-year, benefiting from the first full quarter of Epic Universe.
Peacock losses improved by nearly $220 million year-over-year to just over $200 million in Q3, while Peacock subscribers remained flat following a $3 in-quarter price increase.

The company returned $2.8 billion to shareholders in Q3, including $1.5 billion in share repurchases and $1.2 billion in dividends, contributing to a mid-single-digit year-over-year decline in share count.
Broadband ARPU growth decelerated to 2.6% in Q3, with management expecting ARPU growth to step down more than 1 point in Q4 and continued pressure in early 2026.
Nearly 40% of new broadband connects chose gig-plus speeds in Q3, up approximately 10 percentage points from the start of the year.
Management stated the current plan is to not take a broadband rate increase in early 2026, focusing instead on transitioning customers to new simplified pricing packages.
Graham delivered record fiscal 2026 revenue of $245 million (up 17%), record orders of $359 million, and a record backlog of $533 million, up 29% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x.

Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $285-$295 million (18% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $35-$40 million, representing 44% growth at the midpoint, with gross margin expected at 24.5%-25.5%.

Q4 gross margin compressed to 22.7% from 27% a year earlier due to a higher mix of lower-margin defense revenue with greater material content, lower aftermarket sales, and FLAC Tech purchase accounting amortization.
Q4 adjusted EPS declined to $0.33 from $0.43 year-over-year, while full-year adjusted EPS rose 13% to $1.40 from $1.24.
Approximately 35-40% of the $533 million backlog is expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months, providing substantial visibility into fiscal 2027.

Graham received a $50 million strategic investment from accounts advised by T. Rowe Price (based on the 20-day average closing price as of April 13, 2026), used $13 million to repay debt, and now has over $100 million of available liquidity for organic and inorganic growth.

FLAC Tech, acquired at the end of January, contributed $2.8 million to Q4 sales, currently operates at a ~10% adjusted EBITDA margin, and was burdened by purchase accounting amortization expected to decline going forward.

Defense revenue grew 21% in fiscal 2026, driven by new program wins (including the competitively won Columbia-class submarine air turbine pump) and ramps on directed energy laser and 360-degree radar cooling programs.
Space orders surged 132% year-over-year as customers transition from development/qualification to higher-rate production across launch providers, satellites, lunar landers, and astronaut backpacks.
Fiscal 2027 capex is guided to $18-$22 million (including a new 30,000 sq ft Arvada, Colorado facility), with all strategic investments targeted to exceed the company's 20% ROIC hurdle rate.
Q4 2025 loan originations grew 40% year-over-year to $2.6 billion, with full-year originations growing 33% to nearly $10 billion.
Return on tangible common equity more than tripled to nearly 12% in Q4, with full-year ROTCE of 10.2%.
Full-year 2025 diluted earnings per share more than doubled, growing 158% year-over-year to $1.16.
Net interest income increased 14% year-over-year to $163 million, reaching an all-time high, with net interest margin of 6%, up 56 basis points year-over-year.
LendingClub's credit performance is 40% to 50% better than its competitive set, with net charge-off ratio down 80 basis points year-over-year.
Full-year 2026 guidance projects loan originations of $11.6 billion to $12.6 billion (21% to 31% year-over-year growth) and diluted EPS of $1.65 to $1.80 (42% to 55% year-over-year growth).
The company initiated its first direct forward flow agreement with a top U.S. insurance company in Q4, adding to previously announced agreements with BlackRock and Blue Owl.
Total deposits reached $9.8 billion, up 8% year-over-year, while total assets grew to $11.6 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
Under the $100 million share repurchase program announced in November, the company deployed approximately $12 million in Q4 at an average share price of $17.65.
The company is entering the $0.5 trillion home improvement financing market, with technology acquisition completed and first distribution partnership signed, targeting a mid-year 2026 launch.
Q1 2026 total revenue reached $184 million, up 43% on a spot basis and 37% FX-neutral, including 7 points of organic contribution from Sertifi.
Adjusted EBITDA was $39 million with a 21.4% margin, expanding 452 basis points year-over-year and exceeding the upper end of guidance.

Adjusted gross margin was 60.1%, down approximately 400 basis points, primarily driven by ~250 bps from Cleveland Clinic and B2B invoice client payment revenue mix, with the remainder from vertical mix shifts.

Flywire raised full-year 2026 guidance to 18%-24% FX-neutral revenue growth and ~175-375 bps of EBITDA margin expansion (reaching ~22.8% at the midpoint), with free cash flow conversion of 70%-75% of adjusted EBITDA.

The company announced an accelerated share repurchase program of up to $50 million, the largest single capital return action in its public company history, bringing total buybacks since launch to $128 million.
Education revenue outside the Big 4 markets (U.S., U.K., Canada, Australia) grew over 40% year-over-year in Q1, with more than 60% of new education clients signed coming from outside those markets.
Cornell University signed a long-term agreement for Flywire's full student financial software suite, and the company signed 3 additional U.K. SFS clients in the quarter.

Management estimates an additional $2.5 billion of payment volume opportunity exists within existing U.S. hospitality (Sertifi) clients alone, with international rollout to Europe and Southeast Asia underway.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for 18%-24% FX-neutral revenue growth and ~75 bps EBITDA margin expansion, below the typical annual rate due to lapping Q1 2025 restructuring savings and deliberate investments in domestic, AI, and Sertifi globalization.

Macro assumptions remain prudent with U.S. student visas modeled down 30%, Canada down 10%, and U.K./Australia roughly flat, while AI is driving ~40% auto-resolution of customer inquiries and a 30% reduction in support handling time and cost per contact.
DT Midstream's 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $1.138 billion, a 17% increase over the prior year, exceeding the increased guidance midpoint.
The Pipeline segment grew 27% in 2025, increasing from 50% of DTM's business at the spin-off to 70% today, the highest among its peer group.
DTM updated its five-year organic project backlog by approximately 50% to $3.4 billion, with pipeline projects comprising approximately 75% of the backlog and roughly $1.6 billion already committed.
The 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range is $1.155 billion to $1.225 billion (6% midpoint growth), and the 2027 early outlook is $1.225 billion to $1.295 billion (6% midpoint growth over 2026).

DTM's portfolio is 95% demand-based contracts with an average contract tenure of eight years, and the company has delivered total shareholder return of approximately 280% since its spin-off nearly five years ago.

LEAP Phase 4 expansion was placed into service early and on budget, increasing LEAP capacity to 2.1 Bcf per day, and LEAP is positioned to benefit from an expected 11 Bcf of LNG demand growth through 2030 with two-thirds served by the Haynesville.

Vector pipeline closed a successful binding open season for an expansion to increase westbound capacity into Chicago by approximately 400 million cubic feet per day, with an expected Q4 2028 in-service date subject to owner approvals.

DTM sees an addressable opportunity of up to 13 Bcf per day and a pathway of 5 to 8 Bcf per day of potential incremental gas demand in the Upper Midwest, driven by approximately 35 gigawatts of coal plant retirements and approximately 50 gigawatts of announced utility large load opportunities.
The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.88 per share, a 7.3% increase from the prior year, with a 2025 dividend coverage ratio of 2.6x versus the company's 2x floor commitment.
Year-end 2026 forecast leverage is 2.9x on-balance sheet and 3.5x proportional, and the company achieved investment-grade credit ratings across all three rating agencies in 2025.
CBRE raised full-year 2026 core EPS guidance to $7.60-$7.80 from prior $7.30-$7.60, implying more than 20% growth at the midpoint.

In the Phase II study of 27 low-grade IDH1-mutant glioma patients, safusidenib demonstrated a median PFS not yet reached, a 12% progression rate at 24 months, and a confirmed ORR of 44%, compared to vorasidenib's 27.7-month median PFS, 41% progression rate at 24 months, and 11% ORR in its 168-patient INDIGO study.
